methodology: Named AI training and inference superclusters compiled from public announcements (company press releases, Reuters, Tom's Hardware, Data Center Dynamics, SemiAnalysis, utility filings) plus cross-reference to GridTilt's own Power Map registry. Tracked, not exhaustive. Power in MW. 'estimated' lists the field names whose values are GridTilt estimates or announced forward targets not yet realized; sourced values are not listed there. gpuCount is null when the accelerator count is not disclosed; we do not invent one. linkedDeal references a deal id in interconnection-queue.json where a tracked nuclear-for-AI deal applies to the site.

clusters.name: Stargate Abilene (OpenAI/Oracle)
clusters.notes: Crusoe/Lancium-built flagship Stargate campus on a 15-year Oracle lease. First two of eight buildings live Sept 2025; 1.2 GW target by mid-2026. GPT-5.5 was trained here. 450k GB200 is the announced full deployment target.

clusters.name: Stargate Milam County (OpenAI/Oracle/SoftBank)
clusters.notes: SoftBank-led Stargate campus; can scale toward ~1.5 GW within 18 months of the Sept 2025 announcement.

clusters.name: Stargate Lordstown (OpenAI/Oracle/SoftBank)
clusters.notes: Redevelopment of the former GM/Foxconn complex; OpenAI/Oracle/SoftBank. Scales toward ~1.5 GW.

clusters.name: Stargate Shackelford (Vantage Frontier)
clusters.notes: Vantage Data Centers' $25B, 1.4 GW Frontier campus (10 buildings) tied to the Stargate platform. First facility H2 2026.

clusters.name: Stargate Dona Ana / Project Jupiter (OpenAI/Oracle)
clusters.notes: Dona Ana County NM Stargate site (developer STACK Infrastructure), tied to the BorderPlex 'Project Jupiter' build. OpenAI describes it as 'more than a gigawatt'; Epoch AI lists up to ~2.2 GW full build-out. Now reported under construction. We hold the conservative ~1 GW figure as an estimate.

clusters.name: Stargate Michigan (Saline Township)
clusters.notes: OpenAI/Oracle/Related Digital Stargate campus on 250 acres, roughly 1.4 GW supplied by DTE Energy with project-financed battery storage. Construction began in early 2026 after a contested local vote. Part of the 4.5 GW Oracle-OpenAI Stargate expansion.

clusters.name: xAI Colossus (Memphis)
clusters.notes: Built in 122 days; ~150k H100 + 50k H200 + 30k GB200 (~230k). Power has grown past the early 150-250 MW: ~250 MW grid plus 35 on-site gas turbines (~420 MW), so ~500 MW is the better current figure. The wider Memphis complex (Colossus 1+2+a third building) is cited near 2 GW / ~555k GPUs as of early 2026; that aggregate is not attributed here.

clusters.name: xAI Colossus 2 (Southaven)
clusters.notes: First gigawatt-scale single datacenter; began operations ~Jan 2026 and is ramping (Google/SpaceX agreed to rent capacity here in June 2026). ~350 MW is a grounded current estimate from cooling-capacity analysis vs the ~1 GW launch claim; 41 on-site gas turbines approved Mar 2026 back the path to ~1.2 GW. Compute hall is Memphis (Whitehaven) TN; power generation is Southaven MS.

clusters.name: Meta Prometheus (New Albany)
clusters.notes: Meta's first ~1 GW supercluster, online 2026. Ohio Power Siting Board approved two 200 MW on-site gas plants targeting Q3 2026.

clusters.name: Meta Hyperion (Richland Parish)
clusters.notes: Meta's largest campus: up to 5 GW across ~4M sq ft on 2,250 acres. Construction since late 2024 through 2030; ~1.5 GW interim target by end 2027. Powered by 10 Entergy gas plants.

clusters.name: Meta Pike County (Oklo SMR)
clusters.notes: Meta AI campus tied to the Meta-Oklo Pike County arrangement (prepayments + offtake). Power tracked as the nuclear deal meta-oklo-pike. Capacity is an estimate.

clusters.name: Microsoft Fairwater (Mount Pleasant)
clusters.notes: First building went operational June 23, 2026. Microsoft's We Energies / Wisconsin PSC filing puts Phase 1 power at ~400 MW, with the two-phase single site near 900 MW; hundreds of thousands of GB200/GB300. The wider Mount Pleasant complex is expanding across more buildings (multi-GW long term). Single-site MW tracked here; the full campus is larger.

clusters.name: Microsoft Fairwater (Atlanta)
clusters.notes: Two-story GPU building, ~800k sq ft, ~300 MW, 140 kW/rack, GB200/GB300. Part of Microsoft's >2 GW multi-site Fairwater 'AI superfactory'.

clusters.name: AWS Project Rainier (Anthropic)
clusters.notes: ~500k Trainium2 chips live for Anthropic (Oct 2025), scaling past 1M by end 2025. $11B, 1,200 acres, ultimate ~2.2 GW. Anthropic-Amazon partnership targets up to 5 GW of new compute.

clusters.name: AWS Susquehanna (Talen BTM)
clusters.notes: AWS campus drawing behind-the-meter power from the Susquehanna nuclear plant under the Talen-AWS agreement. Power tracked as the signed deal susquehanna-aws (up to 1,920 MW).

clusters.name: AWS Madison County (Canton)
clusters.notes: AWS's large Mississippi AI campus near Canton (Entergy/MISO). Capacity estimated; cross-referenced from GridTilt's Power Map registry.

clusters.name: Google Council Bluffs (TPU)
clusters.notes: Major Google TPU site in Iowa, anchor for the Google-Anthropic 1M-TPU deal capacity. The NextEra-Google Duane Arnold restart (601 MW, MISO/Iowa) would back Google's Iowa load but is not yet in GridTilt's tracked nuclear deal set, so linkedDeal is null. Per-site TPU counts undisclosed; power estimated.

clusters.name: Google The Dalles (TPU)
clusters.notes: Long-running Google campus on Columbia River hydro, expanded for TPU capacity. Per-site accelerator count and MW not disclosed; figures estimated.

clusters.name: Google Dorchester County (TPU)
clusters.notes: Google South Carolina AI campus (Santee Cooper/SERC). Capacity estimated; cross-referenced from GridTilt's Power Map registry.

clusters.name: Google Clarksville (Kairos SMR)
clusters.notes: Google Tennessee campus in the TVA footprint. The Google-Kairos Hermes 2 SMR (500 MW, Oak Ridge TN, TVA) is tracked as google-kairos-hermes2. Capacity estimated.

clusters.name: Google Pryor Creek (TPU)
clusters.notes: Google Oklahoma AI campus (SPP). Capacity estimated; cross-referenced from GridTilt's Power Map registry.

clusters.name: CoreWeave Ellendale (Applied Digital)

clusters.name: CoreWeave Mebane
clusters.notes: CoreWeave North Carolina site (Duke/SERC). Capacity estimated; cross-referenced from GridTilt's Power Map registry.

clusters.name: CoreWeave / NVIDIA Secaucus
clusters.notes: CoreWeave/NVIDIA northern New Jersey site (PJM). Power estimated; cross-referenced from GridTilt's Power Map registry.

clusters.name: Tesla Cortex 1 (Giga Texas)
clusters.notes: Cortex 1 training cluster at Giga Texas for FSD/Optimus: ~100k H100/H200, ~130 MW, at full capacity since mid-2025. The separate Cortex 2 expansion is tracked as its own entry. GPU count estimated.

clusters.name: Nebius Kansas City (Patmos)
clusters.notes: Nebius's first US availability zone at the Patmos KC data center; 5 MW initial, up to 40 MW, ~35k GPUs (H200 then Blackwell). GPU count estimated.

clusters.name: Nebius Independence (Eastgate)
clusters.notes: Nebius's gigawatt-scale campus at the Eastgate Commerce Center outside Kansas City, now approved for up to ~1.2 GW (up from 800 MW). Nebius also has smaller US sites (NJ, a second PA campus) not tracked here.

clusters.name: QTS Cedar Rapids (Blackstone)
clusters.notes: Blackstone-owned QTS's ~$10B Cedar Rapids campus, Iowa's largest economic-development project. Developer-operated; tenant and accelerator counts not disclosed; capacity estimated.

clusters.name: Meta Beaver Dam
clusters.notes: Meta Wisconsin AI campus (MISO). Capacity estimated; cross-referenced from GridTilt's Power Map registry.

clusters.name: Meta Eagle Mountain
clusters.notes: Meta Utah campus (Rocky Mountain Power/WECC) expanded for AI. Power estimated; cross-referenced from GridTilt's Power Map registry.

clusters.name: AWS Northlake
clusters.notes: AWS north Texas AI hub (ERCOT). Capacity estimated; cross-referenced from GridTilt's Power Map registry.

clusters.name: AWS Puget Sound (X-energy SMR)
clusters.notes: AWS Washington footprint. The X-energy + Energy Northwest Cascade SMR project (960 MW, WA) sits in the same region but is not yet in GridTilt's tracked nuclear deal set, so linkedDeal is null. Capacity estimated; cross-referenced from GridTilt's Power Map registry.

clusters.name: Project Jade (Cheyenne)
clusters.notes: The Cheyenne 'Project Jade' campus (formerly Crusoe + Tallgrass). Crusoe paused and exited development ~April-June 2026 (reportedly after Google, the customer, raised cost/timeline concerns); Tallgrass continues the power side. Grew to 2.7 GW, with headroom toward 10 GW. Data-center developer now undisclosed.

clusters.name: Crusoe Goodnight Campus
clusters.notes: Crusoe AI campus near Claude TX (Armstrong County), anchor customer Google. ~530 MW phase 1 plus ~500 MW phase 2, powered by ~933 MW of off-grid on-site gas turbines. Capacity is the announced full build-out.

clusters.name: Crusoe Abilene II (Microsoft)
clusters.notes: Crusoe's second Abilene campus (900 MW, two ~336 MW IT buildings), built for Microsoft, with behind-the-meter on-site gas plus battery. Distinct from and adjacent to the Oracle/OpenAI Stargate Abilene campus. First building targeted mid-2027.

clusters.name: Stargate Wisconsin (Vantage Lighthouse)
clusters.notes: Vantage Data Centers' 'Lighthouse' campus in Port Washington WI, a Stargate site for OpenAI/Oracle. ~902 MW IT capacity (Epoch lists ~1.3 GW gross build-out); broke ground Dec 2025, completion expected 2028.

clusters.name: Meta El Paso (Project Seafox)
clusters.notes: Meta's ~$10B, 1 GW El Paso AI campus ('Project Seafox'); broke ground Oct 2025, ~1 GW by 2028. ~366 MW of on-site modular gas generation targeted by 2027 plus grid (El Paso Electric / WECC). Accelerator details undisclosed.

clusters.name: Meta Temple
clusters.notes: Meta's Temple TX (Bell County) campus, originally started 2022, paused, then redesigned for AI and resumed; ~1 GW planned, phased late 2026 into 2027, 100% renewable commitment. MW timing is an estimate; accelerator details undisclosed.

clusters.name: Microsoft Pecos (Project Kilby)
clusters.notes: Microsoft's ~2 GW data-center campus in Pecos TX (Reeves County), powered behind-the-meter by a Chevron/Engine No.1 gas plant (up to ~2.67 GW generation; 20-year PPA signed June 2026, FID expected end 2026). The 2 GW here is the disclosed compute target, distinct from generation. First power ~2028.

clusters.name: Nscale Cedarvale (Barstow)
clusters.notes: Nscale's Cedarvale campus in Barstow TX (Ward County), leasing from Ionic Digital, supplying Microsoft. ~234 MW firm phase 1 scaling toward ~1.2 GW (Microsoft option), ~104,000 NVIDIA GB300; phased from Q3 2026. Full capacity is a scale-to target (estimated).

clusters.name: Galaxy Helios (Dickens County)
clusters.notes: Galaxy Digital's Helios campus in Dickens County TX (former bitcoin-mining site), with 800 MW fully committed to CoreWeave under a 15-year lease (+1.7 GW under study). First power tranche energizing early 2026.

clusters.name: IREN Sweetwater Hub
clusters.notes: IREN's two-site Sweetwater TX hub (Sweetwater 1 ~1.4 GW + Sweetwater 2 ~600 MW = ~2 GW). SW1 grid-energized May 2026 with IT ramping; SW2 in construction (~2027). NVIDIA GB300 under a $9.7B Microsoft capacity deal.

clusters.name: IREN Childress
clusters.notes: IREN's Childress TX site. The AI portion (Horizon 1-4, direct-to-chip liquid, NVIDIA GB300) is ~200 MW critical IT; Horizon 1 (~50 MW IT) energized Q4 2025 and is live, with H2-4 through H2 2026. The wider 750 MW site is mostly legacy bitcoin and is not counted here.

clusters.name: Applied Digital Polaris Forge 2 (Harwood)
clusters.notes: Applied Digital's second North Dakota AI campus ('Polaris Forge 2') near Harwood/Fargo, ~280 MW initial and scalable, on wind-heavy MISO grid; broke ground Sept 2025, initial capacity 2026. Separate from the Ellendale campus that hosts CoreWeave.

clusters.name: TeraWulf Lake Mariner
clusters.notes: TeraWulf's Lake Mariner campus in Barker NY (former coal site), hosting HPC for Core42/G42 and a Google-backed Fluidstack expansion. ~438 MW HPC contracted (up to ~750 MW), first ~60 MW IT live Q1 2026, on predominantly zero-carbon NY grid.

clusters.name: Cipher Black Pearl (AWS)
clusters.notes: Cipher Mining's Black Pearl campus near Wink TX (Winkler County), leased to AWS for 15 years: 300 MW gross / ~216 MW critical IT, ERCOT grid; Phase I targeted Q4 2026, full ramp Q1 2027.

clusters.name: Stack Stafford Technology Campus
clusters.notes: Stack Infrastructure's ~1.1 GW campus in Stafford County VA (19 buildings, six 300 MW Dominion substations, ~$4B), in the PJM/Northern Virginia corridor; first phase 2027. Anchor tenant not named.

clusters.name: QTS Van Wert
clusters.notes: QTS (Blackstone) ~$10B Van Wert OH campus (902 acres, up to 7 buildings, ~500 MW), AEP grid with closed-loop cooling; announced May 2026, first building ~Q1 2029. Early-stage, anchor not named.

clusters.name: Tesla Cortex 2 (Giga Texas)
clusters.notes: Tesla's Cortex 2 expansion at Giga Texas: first ~250 MW phase live ~April 2026, full ~500 MW targeted mid-2026, ~100k additional H100/H200, Megapack-backed. Combined Giga Texas (Cortex 1+2) is cited near ~230k GPUs. GPU and current rated MW are estimates.

clusters.name: Meta Lebanon Data Center (LEAP District)
clusters.energySource: grid (matched 100% clean energy via PPAs); closed-loop liquid cooling
clusters.notes: Meta's second Indiana campus, broke ground Feb 11, 2026 in the LEAP Innovation/Research District ~30 mi NW of Indianapolis. ~$10B investment, ~4M sq ft across 13 buildings (10 data center structures) on 1,500 acres. AI-optimized, 1 GW capacity at full build-out, closed-loop liquid cooling. Operator states campus comes online between late 2027 and early 2028; onlineDate set to 2028 conservatively (estimated). plannedPowerMW is the disclosed 1 GW target.

clusters.name: Meta Jeffersonville Data Center (River Ridge)
clusters.notes: Meta's first Indiana campus, announced Jan 2024, ~$800M, ~700,000 sq ft on a 619-acre site in River Ridge Commerce Center near Louisville. Under construction with planned 2026 operations; expansions through 2029. Renewable-matched, LEED Gold. Meta did not disclose MW; third-party tracker (datacentermap) lists ~407 MW, so plannedPowerMW set to ~400 (estimated).

clusters.name: Meta Kansas City Data Center (Northland)
clusters.notes: Live and serving traffic as of Aug 20, 2025; Meta's first Missouri data center. ~$1B investment, 1.4M+ sq ft across three data center buildings plus a warehouse in the Northland (near I-435/Hwy 169). LEED Gold, electricity matched 100% clean/renewable. Part of Meta's AI-optimized data center build path. MW not disclosed by operator; rated/planned are conservative GridTilt estimates.

clusters.name: Meta DeKalb Data Center
clusters.notes: Meta DeKalb campus at 515 E Gurler Road; first building online 2022, additional buildings reached operational status Dec 2024. 2.3M+ sq ft, up to five data center buildings, >$1B invested, 100% renewable matched. Supports Meta's compute including AI workloads. Note: the specific NVIDIA H100 / MTIA chip claim could not be confirmed in cited sources, so chipType set to unknown and gpuCount null. MW figures are GridTilt estimates; operator did not publish site MW.

clusters.name: Meta Fort Worth Data Center (AllianceTexas)
clusters.notes: Meta's existing $1B+ hyperscale campus in AllianceTexas, ~170+ acres, 2.5M+ sq ft across multiple buildings, drawing on wind energy; expanded repeatedly. Distinct from Meta's tracked El Paso and Temple TX sites. Supports Meta's core platforms and growing AI compute. Third-party tracker (datacentermap) lists ~200 MW; figures treated as GridTilt estimates since not officially disclosed.

clusters.name: Meta Montgomery Data Center
clusters.notes: Announced May 2024 (~$800M), expanded Sept 2025 to bring total Montgomery investment to $1.5B and campus to 1.3M+ sq ft (two more buildings). AI-optimized, off I-65 across from the Hyundai plant. Expected online end of 2026 (estimated). plannedPowerMW is a GridTilt estimate; MW not disclosed.

clusters.name: Applied Digital Adair County
clusters.energySource: grid (MISO / MidAmerican Energy; adjacent NextEra wind substation)
clusters.notes: Applied Digital's proposed ~200 MW data center southeast of Adair, Adair County, IA (~$1.5B, two ~300k sqft buildings adjacent to a NextEra wind substation; connects to MidAmerican Energy grid, MISO). Announced 2024, faced local zoning/setback opposition; still in planning/permitting. Pre-construction, ratedPowerMW=0. Workload changed training->mixed (operator has not disclosed a workload split). Distinct from tracked ND Applied Digital sites.

clusters.name: Hut 8 Beacon Point AI Data Center Campus
clusters.chipType: NVIDIA GB-class (designed to NVIDIA DSX reference architecture)
clusters.notes: 525-acre greenfield site in Nueces County near Corpus Christi (Robstown, FM 1694, adjacent to Lon C. Hill power station). 1,000 MW interconnection secured. First phase: 15-year $9.8B lease (up to ~$25B with options) for 352 MW IT to an investment-grade tenant, built to NVIDIA DSX spec. Initial energization Q1 2027, first data hall Q3 2027. Jacobs is EPCM. Part of Hut 8's multi-GW pipeline. ratedPowerMW=0 (construction).

clusters.name: Riot Platforms Corsicana AI/HPC Campus
clusters.notes: 858-acre campus in Navarro County, up to 1 GW ERCOT-approved (400 MW currently bitcoin). Jan 2025 Riot halted Phase II bitcoin expansion and engaged Altman Solon to evaluate AI/HPC use of the remaining ~600 MW; SEC filing designates an initial 600 MW for AI/HPC. Has since filed a ~$400M TDLR permit ('Project Ditto', ~335k sqft, construction from Apr 2026, completion targeted 2028) and expanded land +238 acres. No named AI tenant yet and exact AI-vs-bitcoin use of the new building is not fully specified; conversion not guaranteed. chipType cleared (none disclosed). onlineDate set to 2028 per permit completion target.

clusters.name: Riot Platforms Rockdale AI Data Center (AMD)
clusters.chipType: AMD Instinct (AMD is the lease tenant)
clusters.notes: Distinct from the Stargate/Milam County (OpenAI/Oracle) roster entry: this is Riot's own Rockdale bitcoin-mining site (Milam County, ~700 MW interconnection) being converted to AI. Jan 2026 Riot bought 200 acres ($96M) and signed a 10-yr Data Center Lease with AMD: initial 25 MW (phased Jan-May 2026), AMD exercised +25 MW (=50 MW), with expansion option + ROFR to 200 MW total (~$1B revenue if all extensions exercised). Building retrofit underway; initial phases may be energizing in 2026. First named AI-tenant deal for Riot. ratedPowerMW=0 (campus build-out in progress).

clusters.name: CleanSpark Austin County AI Data Center Campus
clusters.energySource: grid (ERCOT); natural gas behind-the-meter under evaluation
clusters.notes: Oct 2025: CleanSpark (bitcoin miner) acquired rights to ~271 acres in Austin County, TX (between Houston and Austin; Bellville/Austin County area) and signed long-term power agreements totaling 285 MW for a next-gen AI/HPC data center campus on a regional fiber backbone. Substation construction underway and long-lead items secured; energization of 200+ MW expected H1 2027. First major AI/HPC campus for CleanSpark. location.city corrected from 'Austin County' (a county, not a city) to Bellville (Austin County seat) with adjusted coords. chipType cleared (none disclosed). ratedPowerMW=0 (construction).

clusters.name: Soluna Project Kati (Kati 2 AI/HPC)
clusters.notes: Soluna's largest site; broke ground Sept 18, 2025 in Willacy County (Rio Grande Valley), 166 MW two-phase, wind-supported (EDF Renewables/Masdar/Spring Lane). Kati 1 (83 MW) is bitcoin hosting (48 MW for Galaxy + 35 MW Soluna), coming online early 2026; Kati 2 (83 MW) is the AI/HPC phase, co-developed with Metrobloks (Jan 2026). plannedPowerMW=166 is the full campus build-out; the AI/HPC slice is ~83-100 MW. Dual-purpose crypto-to-AI campus. Power figure is the DC's contracted/co-located capacity, not wind-farm nameplate.

clusters.name: Soluna Project Dorothy 3 AI/HPC Campus
clusters.notes: Planned 300+ MW renewable-powered AI/HPC campus on 300 newly acquired acres adjacent to Soluna's existing Dorothy 1/2 wind-powered facilities and Briscoe Wind Farm near Silverton (Briscoe County), West Texas. In 2026 Soluna consolidated full ownership of Dorothy 1A/1B to clear the path for AI/HPC conversion; definitive land purchase agreement signed and formal commercial negotiations started with at least one prospective tenant. Pre-construction. plannedPowerMW reflects the DC target, not wind nameplate.

clusters.name: Bitfarms/Keel Panther Creek HPC/AI Campus
clusters.energySource: grid (PJM); former Panther Creek waste-coal power plant site
clusters.notes: Carbon County, PA campus (former Panther Creek waste-coal/cogen plant acquired by Bitfarms, now rebranded Keel Infrastructure). Aug 2025: partnership with T5 Data Centers for a 350 MW HPC/AI campus (four 315k sqft buildings on 90 acres + secondary phase); Oct 2025: $300M Macquarie project financing + $50M draw. Nesquehoning planning commission gave conditional/preliminary approval (Feb-May 2026); construction targeted to start mid-2026, phase 1 by year-end 2026. Early-stage construction, crypto-miner-to-AI conversion. Status borderline construction/announced.

clusters.name: Keel Infrastructure Sharon AI Data Center
clusters.energySource: grid (PJM); former Westinghouse Electric plant site
clusters.notes: Mercer County, PA. Keel (formerly Bitfarms) operates a ~30 MW data center on an 18-acre former Westinghouse Electric site (Clark St, acquired Oct 2025) and in May 2026 received Sharon zoning-board approval to expand to a 110 MW AI data center, with two 80 MW substations targeted for end-2026; plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin. Conditions include 70 dB noise cap and no river water; still needs county/city sign-off. Distinct from Panther Creek. ratedPowerMW=30 is the existing operating data center; 110 MW is the announced AI build-out.

clusters.name: Bitdeer Knoxville AI Data Center Conversion
clusters.notes: Bitdeer's ~86 MW Knoxville bitcoin site (Carpenter Creek LLC, 5101 S. National Dr) is being partially converted: 35 MW of capacity into an AI data center, completion targeted early Q4 2026. AI design docs/building permit submitted, long-lead equipment ordered, mining rigs being decommissioned. Crypto-to-AI conversion within an existing campus. plannedPowerMW=35 reflects the AI slice, not the full 86 MW site.

clusters.name: Bitdeer Shalersville (Turnpike Commerce Center) Data Center Campus
clusters.notes: Portage County, OH: Bitdeer (with developer Geis Cos.) under contract for ~257 acres at the Turnpike Commerce Center, Shalersville Township, to build what would be its largest US facility - 15 buildings, initial 150 MW scaling to 750 MW, ~5-year build, $300M+ ex-compute. Presented publicly June 16, 2026; facing local pushback (power/water/noise) and a township data-center moratorium running to ~early November. Not yet approved - announced/pre-approval stage.

clusters.name: Northern Data Ardent Pittsburgh AI/HPC Data Center
clusters.chipType: NVIDIA (GPU/high-density AI compute; D2C and RDHx liquid cooling)
clusters.notes: Northern Data (Northern Bitcoin/Whinstone crypto roots) opened its first North American Ardent AI/HPC data center in the Pittsburgh metro (McKees Rocks, 615 McMichael Rd; 41k sqft / 7.5 acres), June 4, 2025. ~20 MW total via phased build, ~5 MW operational at launch scaling to 20 MW by H2 2025; 135 kW+ rack densities, direct-to-chip + rear-door-HX liquid cooling, target PUE ~1.15. ratedPowerMW=5 reflects live capacity at opening (estimated, conservative); 20 MW is the planned full build. Northern Data being acquired by Rumble.

clusters.name: Aligned Conesville AI Campus
clusters.energySource: grid (former AEP Conesville coal plant brownfield; AEP Ohio)
clusters.notes: Announced July 24, 2025. Multi-building mega-scale AI campus on a 197-acre brownfield parcel inside Conesville Industrial Park (Coshocton County), adjacent to the former AEP Conesville 2GW coal power plant (decommissioned 2020). Planned up to four buildings; Aligned's third Ohio campus. A foundational customer is secured for the first data center; initial capacity targeted mid-2026. Operator did not disclose total MW; plannedPowerMW ~250MW is a GridTilt order-of-magnitude estimate for a multi-building Aligned campus. Verified via search June 2026.

clusters.name: Vantage NV1 Nevada AI Campus
clusters.notes: Announced July 15, 2025. ~$3B, 224MW AI campus in Storey County (Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center, outside Reno) on ~137 acres; four multi-story data centers, >1M sq ft. Vantage's first Nevada site and eighth North American market. Engineered for AI/high-density (360-720 W/sq ft), supports air-cooled and liquid-cooled GPU loads. First two buildings fully leased; first building scheduled to open Q2 2026. 224MW is the operator-disclosed campus figure. Verified via search June 2026.

clusters.name: Aligned Project Caprock
clusters.notes: Broke ground April 9, 2026. 540MW, 313-acre next-generation campus in Hale County just outside Abernathy, northwest Texas; 1.65M sq ft across six facilities; DeltaFlow closed-loop liquid cooling for AI/hyperscale workloads. First building (LBB-01) targeted Q1 2027. Xcel Energy (SPS) is utility partner; in SPP footprint, separate from ERCOT. ~$5B regional impact. 540MW is operator-disclosed. Verified via search June 2026.

clusters.name: Compass Meridian Campus
clusters.notes: Announced Jan 2025; $10B hyperscale campus in Meridian, Lauderdale County (I-20/59 Industrial Park); eight data centers (~40MW IT each, ~320MW total IT) of ~250,000 sq ft each, built over ~8 years. Mississippi Power to supply ~500MW total grid power to the campus (plannedPowerMW reflects this disclosed power-supply figure, which exceeds the 320MW IT load). Customer not disclosed; built for hyperscale/AI demand. Distinct from AWS Canton MS. Verified via search June 2026.

clusters.name: PowerHouse-Provident DFW Hyperscale Campus
clusters.notes: JV announced Feb 25, 2025. 768-acre DFW hyperscale campus just outside Grand Prairie in northern Ellis County, between Dallas and Fort Worth. On-site 1.8GW switchyard; first 500MW tranche approved through ERCOT; 24 buildings across three phases. First building slated to energize May 2026. plannedPowerMW=1800 reflects the disclosed 1.8GW switchyard capacity (a proxy for full build-out; total DC load not separately disclosed), flagged estimated. Replaced an invalid second source (datacenterknowledge hub did not mention this project) with the DCD article. Verified via search June 2026.

clusters.name: Prime PHX01 Avondale Campus
clusters.notes: Broke ground May 21, 2026 on first three buildings (~48MW/267,000 sq ft each) of PHX01, a five-building, 240MW IT, ~1.3M sq ft, 66.5-acre AI campus in Avondale (Greater Phoenix); $3B investment. All three initial buildings pre-leased to a single unnamed leading hyperscaler (~144MW). AI/HPC high-density design with closed-loop zero-water cooling. Verified via BusinessWire and Prime's own newsroom.

clusters.name: Tract Buckeye Data Center Park
clusters.energySource: grid (APS; new power infrastructure in planning)
clusters.notes: Tract closed on ~2,069 acres in Buckeye (Maricopa County) for $136M for a gigawatt-scale, master-planned data center park; ~$20B, up to ~20M sq ft across as many as 40 data centers, with utility (APS) work to support up to 1.8GW. Named developer with site secured and power in planning; tenants not yet named, so treated as announced. 15-18 year horizon. plannedPowerMW = announced 1.8GW utility-support target (estimated).

clusters.name: Switch Citadel Campus (Tahoe Reno)
clusters.notes: Operational Switch flagship colo campus in the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center (Storey County, near Sparks/Reno), opened 2017; ~1,000-2,000 acres, master-planned to 7.2M sq ft and up to ~650MW. Tahoe Reno 1 supports up to ~130MW (used as conservative operational ratedPowerMW, estimated). AI-positioned via Switch's EVO AI Factory / NVIDIA Omniverse DSX architecture for high-density GPU racks; TR2/TR3 under construction. Medium confidence as an AI-buildout entry since it is an existing colo campus being upgraded for AI; ratedPowerMW and full plannedPowerMW are estimates.

clusters.name: Sailfish Comanche Circle
clusters.energySource: behind-the-meter natural gas, with reserved land for SMR and solar
clusters.notes: 2,600-acre, nine-campus data center community near Tolar (Hood County), ~45 mi SW of Fort Worth in the DFW metro, <1 mi from Comanche Peak nuclear plant with 345kV access (ERCOT/Oncor). Published as up to 5 GW total; Phase 1 = five campuses ~3.2GW. plannedPowerMW = 5,000 (full build-out target, estimated). Up to 600MW behind-the-meter gas within 24 months; 400 acres reserved for SMR/solar. In talks with prospective tenants and seeking funding; pre-construction so ratedPowerMW 0.

clusters.name: Texas Critical Data Centers (TCDC)
clusters.notes: 438-acre AI/HPC campus in Ector County near Odessa, Permian Basin; New Era now owns 100% (bought out Sharon AI). Engineering/permitting/site-prep underway, full construction ~2026, so early construction. Well-sourced data center figure is 250 MW (DCF describes a 250MW net-zero campus); plannedPowerMW = 250 (estimated). Newer Jan 2026 framing markets a scale-to '1+ GW' campus (kept conservative at 250). Phase 1 ~100 MW targeted by Dec 2026. EYP full-scope engineering; Stream Data Centers JV. ratedPowerMW 0 (no live IT load). GPU count not disclosed.

clusters.name: Prometheus Hyperscale Evanston (WY-1)
clusters.energySource: fully islanded natural gas microgrid; low-carbon/nuclear SMR + battery roadmap; closed-loop liquid cooling
clusters.notes: Status corrected construction->announced: Uinta County granted only a conditional use permit (June 2026); construction has NOT begun and is anticipated to start within six months of final permitting, built out over 48-60 months. Flagship ~506-acre campus ~12 mi east of Evanston, approved at 1.25GW with a stated path to 5GW; fully islanded gas microgrid, closed-loop cooling. plannedPowerMW = 1,250 (approved/announced power figure, estimated). ratedPowerMW 0 (pre-construction). GPU count not disclosed.

clusters.name: Prometheus Hyperscale Casper (Natrona County)
clusters.energySource: on-site firm natural gas with point-source + direct air carbon capture (carbon-negative)
clusters.notes: Second Prometheus Hyperscale site near Casper in Natrona/Converse County (distinct from Evanston WY-1). Oct 2025 partnership with Spiritus (Orchard Power, 1.5 GW on-site firm gas) and Casper Carbon Capture targets up to 1.5 GW of IT-ready capacity over multiple phases (carbon-negative). plannedPowerMW = 1,500 (announced IT target, estimated). First IT-ready power targeted ~2026, full campus ~2028. Pre-construction so ratedPowerMW 0.

clusters.name: Poolside Project Horizon (Longfellow Ranch)
clusters.energySource: behind-the-meter aero-derivative natural gas turbines (Permian gas)
clusters.notes: 2 GW AI training campus on 568 acres of Longfellow Ranch near Fort Stockton (Pecos County), distinct from Pecos city / Microsoft Kilby. Eight 250-MW phases; plannedPowerMW = 2,000 (announced target, estimated). CoreWeave had been anchor for the first 250 MW (expandable to 500 MW) with a committed 40,000+ GB300 NVL72 GPUs, but CoreWeave terminated the 15-year lease in late March 2026 after Poolside's ~$2B Series C failed to close; that GPU/chip commitment is now void, so gpuCount set to null and chipType cleared. Poolside is now seeking new partners; site idle. ratedPowerMW 0.

clusters.name: Fleet Data Centers South Valley
clusters.energySource: grid (NV Energy) with planned temporary on-site natural gas generation
clusters.notes: Build-to-suit megacampus at the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center (Storey County), on USA Parkway; broke ground June 2026 with Fleet's Peru Ridge campus. Reporting gives the two Fleet campuses a combined 400 MW critical compute; South Valley ~200 MW critical compute (plus ~30 MW utility), used as plannedPowerMW (estimated). 100% leased to a AA-/$3T+-market-cap tenant (reported as Nvidia) on a ~197-month triple-net lease. Online ~Q4 2027. ratedPowerMW 0.

clusters.name: Fleet Data Centers Peru Ridge
clusters.energySource: grid (NV Energy) with planned temporary on-site natural gas generation
clusters.notes: Renamed from candidate 'Peru Shelf': Fleet's actual compute campus is Peru Ridge at 2300 Peru Drive, McCarran (Storey County), one of the two Fleet campuses that broke ground June 2026. (Peru Shelf Technology Park is the adjacent ~810 MW Tract land/utility park, not the named compute campus.) Peru Ridge is part of the combined 400 MW critical compute across the two Fleet campuses; plannedPowerMW = ~200 critical compute (estimated). Initial power delivery late 2026/early 2027, online ~Q3 2027. ratedPowerMW 0. Anchor not separately disclosed.

clusters.name: Novva Tahoe Reno Data Center
clusters.notes: Launched July 8, 2025 as Novva's fourth completed data center. 300,000 sq ft, 60 MW across six 10 MW halls on 20 acres at the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center (Storey County), fed by an on-site 100 MW NV Energy substation. Water-free cooling, direct-to-chip-compatible for GPU loads. Multi-tenant colo (mixed). Additional capacity coming 2026. ratedPowerMW = 60 (disclosed live build).

clusters.name: Vantage AZ1 Goodyear Campus
clusters.notes: 50-acre AZ1 campus at 45 S Bullard Ave, Goodyear (metro Phoenix), >1M sq ft. Four facilities live/topped out (AZ11, AZ12, AZ13, AZ14) totaling 160 MW; AZ14 added liquid-cooling-capable capacity for next-gen GPU loads. Full build-out is 176 MW of critical IT across five buildings (plannedPowerMW). Multiple buildings operational, so ratedPowerMW set to 160 (conservative sourced estimate of currently delivered critical IT; flagged estimated).

clusters.name: Aligned PHX-13 Glendale Campus
clusters.notes: Verified: groundbreaking April 15, 2025 (multiple sources incl. City of Glendale press release) on PHX-13, first of four planned data centers on a 100-acre Glendale campus (metro Phoenix), >1M sq ft planned. PHX-13 delivers 72MW; Delta-cubed cooling, closed-loop water recycling, AI/hyperscale loads; APS building a new 230kV line. 72MW is the first building; full campus larger. plannedPowerMW reflects the 72MW PHX-13 building only (campus total not separately disclosed), so estimated. No GPU/chip disclosed.

clusters.name: Vantage Millersport Campus (OH2)
clusters.notes: Verified: Vantage's second Ohio campus (OH2), ~28 miles west of Columbus in Millersport, Fairfield County; ~$2.1B announced (NBC4). Distinct from Vantage's New Albany OH1 and from any roster site. ~800MW across up to five single-story buildings (120-250MW each); large behind-the-meter on-site generation, possibly fully on-site powered. Construction expected to start by end of 2025, first building targeted 2027. No GPU/chip disclosed; plannedPowerMW and onlineDate are announced targets.

clusters.name: PowerHouse 95 (PH 95)
clusters.notes: Verified by DCD and PowerHouse releases. PowerHouse Data Centers (American Real Estate Partners) broke ground on PH 95 in Spotsylvania County, VA (I-95 corridor, greater Data Center Alley) on a 145-acre site. Up to 800MW across three 300MW substations; up to eight three-story buildings, 3.5M sq ft; hyperscale/AI. First substation targeted to provide 150MW by Oct 2025; phased deliveries Q3 2025-Q4 2027. Distinct operator and county from roster's Stack Stafford VA. No GPU/chip disclosed.

clusters.name: GridFree South Dallas One
clusters.notes: Verified announcement (late Dec 2025), named developer (Houston-based GridFree AI), Goldman Sachs co-leading financing, Newmark exclusive marketer. South Dallas One in Hill County, ~1 hr south of DFW; first of a planned three-site South Dallas Cluster (~5GW gross, each site >1.5GW). Gas behind-the-meter (100MW modules), industrial chilled-water cooling, deliverable ~24 months from lease signing. Early-stage and speculative: no committed AI tenant and site control not publicly confirmed, but it is a named developer with an announced compute plan, not an anonymous land play. plannedPowerMW and onlineDate are announced targets; no GPU/chip disclosed.

clusters.name: Hut 8 River Bend Campus
clusters.notes: Verified by Louisiana Economic Development, Entergy, Hut 8 PR, and DCD. River Bend AI campus, West Feliciana Parish, LA (St. Francisville; Baton Rouge metro). Up to $10B Phase I. Hut 8 signed a 15-yr, 245MW IT lease ($7.0B TCV) with Fluidstack (lease obligations backstopped by Google; tied to Fluidstack's multi-GW Anthropic partnership), for AI training/inference. Entergy initial 330MW utility capacity, ROFO for +1,000MW; potential to scale beyond 1GW. Initial data hall commissioning Q2 2027. plannedPowerMW (1,000) is the announced expansion ceiling, so estimated; no GPU/chip disclosed by Hut 8.

clusters.name: T5 @ Atlanta IV (ATL IV)
clusters.notes: T5's fourth Atlanta campus (ATL IV) on a 91-acre site in the Palmetto/Fairburn area of South Fulton County, GA. Originally announced Aug 2024 as a scalable-to-300MW, 7-building, 2.95M sq ft campus explicitly designed for advanced AI / high-density compute with rack-level liquid cooling. That application was withdrawn; a scaled-down 3-building plan (~200MW, ~1.32M sq ft along Gullatt Rd) was refiled May 2025 and cleared Atlanta Regional Commission DRI review in Nov 2025. On-site substation expected operational 2026, but data center Phase 1 construction is set to begin Q2 2027 with delivery in 2027, so this is announced/permitted, not yet under construction. plannedPowerMW set to the current scaled ~200MW target (down from original 300MW headline). Distinct from tracked Microsoft Fairwater Atlanta.

clusters.name: Google Red Hawk Campus (Mesa)
clusters.notes: Google's first Arizona data center, 'Red Hawk' on 187 acres at Elliot/Sossaman. Phase 1 (288,530 sq ft) operational July 2025. Phase 2 designed for ~400MW. March 2026 revised filing consolidates remaining phases into a high-density two-building configuration to support generative AI. ratedPowerMW is a conservative GridTilt estimate for the operational phase; 400MW is the announced campus target.

clusters.name: Google Henderson Campus
clusters.notes: 210-acre campus in Henderson's Black Mountain Industrial Park (Clark County), backed by $1.2B+ investment; ~60% of planned shell capacity reached by early 2025. Part of Google's $400M+ 2026 Nevada cloud/AI spend. ratedPowerMW is a conservative GridTilt estimate (no MW disclosed).

clusters.name: Google Red Oak Data Center (Ellis County)
clusters.energySource: ERCOT grid with Texas renewable PPAs
clusters.notes: Second Google North Texas data center (announced 2023) in Red Oak, Ellis County, now confirmed operational; sits alongside Google's Midlothian campus. Part of Google's $40B Texas commitment through 2027. ratedPowerMW is a conservative GridTilt estimate (no MW disclosed).

clusters.name: Google Goodnight Campus (Armstrong County / Crusoe)
clusters.energySource: Texas Panhandle wind (closed-loop cooling), ERCOT grid
clusters.notes: Hyperscale campus on ~1,300 acres near Claude, TX, developed by Crusoe Energy with Google as tenant; construction underway since May 2025, completion ~late 2028/early 2029. Pulls from ERCOT (not the local SPP supply). One of three Texas campuses in Google's $40B build-out. plannedPowerMW is a GridTilt estimate scaled to the 1GW+ co-located complex; the data-center IT load was not separately disclosed.

clusters.name: Google Haskell County Campus (Quantum)
clusters.notes: Two new Google data center campuses in Haskell County (West Texas), one paired with the Quantum Clean Energy Project (640MW solar PV + 1.3GWh storage via Intersect/TPG Rise Climate), targeted completion by end of 2027. plannedPowerMW is a GridTilt estimate; only generation (640MW solar) was disclosed, not the data-center IT load.

clusters.name: Google Lenoir Campus (Caldwell County)
clusters.energySource: Duke Energy grid with renewable PPAs
clusters.notes: One of Google's oldest US campuses (opened ~2008), now a 3.37M sq ft facility. March 2026: $1B two-year expansion to meet AI/cloud demand, building on $1.2B+ already invested. ratedPowerMW/plannedPowerMW are GridTilt estimates (no MW disclosed).

clusters.name: Google Berkeley County Campus (Moncks Corner)
clusters.energySource: Santee Cooper grid with renewable PPAs
clusters.notes: Google's first South Carolina data center (established 2007/08) at Mount Holly Commerce Park, Moncks Corner; $1.3B Berkeley County expansion within Google's $3.3B+ SC commitment. ratedPowerMW/plannedPowerMW are GridTilt estimates (no MW disclosed).

clusters.name: Google Jackson County Campus (Widows Creek)
clusters.energySource: TVA grid (former Widows Creek coal site); Kairos SMR nuclear PPA
clusters.notes: Campus on the former TVA Widows Creek coal-plant site near Bridgeport, operating since 2019, reusing existing transmission. June 2026: $1.5B expansion for generative/agentic AI over 2026-27. Long-term clean power via the Google-TVA-Kairos 50MW SMR deal. ratedPowerMW/plannedPowerMW are GridTilt estimates (no DC MW disclosed).

clusters.name: Google Fort Wayne Campus (Project Zodiac)
clusters.notes: $2B Google campus ('Project Zodiac') near E Tillman/Adams Center Rds, broke ground April 2024, went live Dec 11, 2025; Sept 2025 approval to add five more buildings. Indiana is one of the city-identified states in Google's AI buildout. ratedPowerMW/plannedPowerMW are GridTilt estimates (no MW disclosed).

clusters.name: Google Pine Island Campus (Project Skyway)
clusters.energySource: Xcel Energy wind/solar/storage (1,400MW wind + 200MW solar + 300MW storage)
clusters.notes: Google's first Minnesota data center on a 482-acre tech park at Pine Island (~70mi SE of Minneapolis), ~88 acres for the initial 250,000 sq ft building; CUP approved Jan 2026. Construction halted by a Goodhue County court order (May 2026) pending environmental review. Xcel to add 1,900MW clean generation. plannedPowerMW is a GridTilt estimate of DC load; only generation MW was firmly disclosed.

clusters.name: Google Van Buren Township Campus (Project Cannoli)
clusters.notes: Google confirmed (March 2026) as backer of 'Project Cannoli', a ~1GW hyperscale data center on ~282 acres in Van Buren Township, Wayne County (near Detroit). Awaiting MPSC contested-case review of the DTE supply deal. plannedPowerMW (1,000MW) is the disclosed data-center power requirement; Google to support 1,600MW renewables + 450MW storage separately.

clusters.name: Google Lancaster Campus (Rock Mill)
clusters.energySource: AEP Ohio grid with renewable PPAs
clusters.notes: Google campus on a 120-acre site in Rock Mill Industrial Park (Whiley Rd off US-33), Fairfield County; ground broken 2023, first building completed 2024. Distinct from Google's New Albany and Columbus/Lockbourne central-Ohio campuses. ratedPowerMW/plannedPowerMW are GridTilt estimates (no MW disclosed).

clusters.name: Microsoft Fairwater Atlanta (AI Superfactory)
clusters.notes: Microsoft's second Fairwater AI campus, live October/November 2025 on a 615-acre QTS-developed campus in Fayetteville, Fayette County (south of Atlanta), >1M sq ft, two-story design, 140kW/rack and 1,360kW/row, hundreds of thousands of NVIDIA GB200/GB300 GPUs. No on-site generation/UPS/gensets (relies on grid). Microsoft did not disclose total MW; interconnection.fyi tracker lists 250+ MW (used as conservative estimate). Connected to Wisconsin Fairwater via AI WAN as a distributed superfactory. Distinct from Microsoft's Union City and Palmetto Atlanta-region campuses.

clusters.name: Microsoft San Antonio (Castroville / Medina) Campus
clusters.notes: Microsoft's expanding South Central US footprint west of San Antonio in Medina County. SAT89/SAT90 (2995 US Hwy 90 W, Castroville): two single-story buildings, 489,400 sq ft total, $765M, construction June 2025 to July 2027. Additional SAT80/81/82 at 8844 FM Road and SAT93/SAT94 along County Road 381 (245,000 sq ft each, $350M/building). South Central US region serves Azure cloud and AI demand. No MW disclosed (pre-completion, ratedPowerMW set to 0).

clusters.name: Microsoft Project Ginger West (West Des Moines)
clusters.notes: Hyperscale campus in Polk County, ~188 acres, ~1.8M sq ft across multiple buildings, $1B+ investment, ~207 MW design capacity, early phases ~2026 with full buildout ~2028. Part of Microsoft's West Des Moines cluster (the same metro that hosted the OpenAI GPT-4 training supercomputer); supports cloud and AI workloads. Adopting zero-water cooling for new buildings.

clusters.name: Microsoft Mount Prospect (Chicago) Campus
clusters.notes: $2.5B Microsoft data center campus on the former United Airlines HQ site in Mount Prospect (Cook County), ~1.5M sq ft across three planned buildings. Part of Microsoft's North Central US (Illinois) Azure region buildout, which is adding availability zones by late 2026, supporting cloud and AI demand in Chicagoland. MW not disclosed (set 0). ComEd grid is PJM.

clusters.name: AWS Desper Creek Technology Campus
clusters.notes: Named AWS campus on ~140 acres in Louisa County's Technology Overlay District (south of Route 33, between Mt. Airy Rd and Shannon Hill Rd); up to 8 data center buildings plus a substation. Army Corps / Virginia DEQ permit filed Aug 2025, replacing a withdrawn June 2025 proposal. plannedPowerMW is a GridTilt estimate from 8-building scale; no MW disclosed.

clusters.name: AWS Warrenton Training Center Campus
clusters.notes: AWS operational data center at the Warrenton Training Center in Fauquier County, part of the US-East-1 (Northern Virginia) AI/cloud cluster (Bedrock/Claude, SageMaker, Trainium/Inferentia). Fauquier has eight further data center proposals plus one expansion in the pipeline. ratedPowerMW/plannedPowerMW are conservative GridTilt estimates; operator MW not disclosed.

clusters.name: AWS Salem Township (Susquehanna / Cumulus) Campus
clusters.energySource: nuclear (Susquehanna Steam Electric Station PPA) + grid
clusters.notes: 1,200-acre nuclear-anchored campus (formerly Cumulus) in Salem Township, Luzerne County, bought from Talen for $650M; co-located with the Susquehanna nuclear plant. AWS data-center compute load up to 960 MW (ramping in 120 MW increments, one-time option to cap at 480 MW); plan for 15 data center buildings over a decade. plannedPowerMW = 960 MW compute load (NOT the ~1.9 GW generation PPA). ratedPowerMW reflects early-phase developed capacity (estimate).

clusters.name: AWS Falls Township Bucks County Campus
clusters.notes: Second anchor site of AWS's $20B Pennsylvania investment (announced June 2025), located in Falls Township, Bucks County (Fairless Hills area). Distinct from the Salem Township nuclear campus. plannedPowerMW is a conservative GridTilt estimate; no MW disclosed.

clusters.name: AWS Boardman Bombing Range Road Campus
clusters.energySource: grid (PacifiCorp / Umatilla Electric Co-op) + AWS renewables
clusters.notes: Additional AWS Morrow County campus on the west side of Bombing Range Road, ~1 mi south of Hwy 730 / I-84, near Boardman; 4-5 single-story buildings (~215,461 sqft each) plus water treatment, storage and security buildings. Zoning approved, tax-break filings. Part of AWS's large US-West-2 Oregon AI/cloud footprint. plannedPowerMW is a GridTilt estimate; no MW disclosed.

clusters.name: AWS Wheatfield Campus
clusters.notes: Up to 9-building, 304-acre AWS campus in Wheatfield, Jasper County, near the Schahfer Generating Station; ~$7B, part of Amazon's $15B Northern Indiana program adding 2.4 GW for AI/cloud (NIPSCO territory). Air cooling ~98% of year; AWS pays $1.25B to shield ratepayers. Distinct from the New Carlisle / Project Rainier site. plannedPowerMW is a GridTilt estimate; no per-site MW disclosed.

clusters.name: AWS Hobart Campus
clusters.notes: 500-acre AWS next-gen data center campus in Hobart, Lake County, agreed Nov 2025 within days of Amazon's $15B Northern Indiana AI announcement; construction targeted spring 2026. NIPSCO power deal saving ratepayers ~$1B over 15 years. Distinct from New Carlisle and Wheatfield. plannedPowerMW is a GridTilt estimate; no per-site MW disclosed.

clusters.name: AWS Mesa Elliot/Pecos Road Campuses
clusters.notes: Two AWS Mesa campuses in the Phoenix metro: Elliot Road (42.9 ac, two ~227K sqft buildings, adjacent to Apple's Mesa DC) and 10464 E. Pecos Road (71.3 ac, two ~227K sqft buildings, near Legacy Park). Land bought Dec 2021; plans filed with Mesa planning. SRP grid. plannedPowerMW is a conservative GridTilt estimate across the four buildings; no MW disclosed.

clusters.name: AWS Warren County (Vicksburg) Campus
clusters.notes: AWS next-generation data center campus in Warren County (Vicksburg), $3B, announced Nov 2025; largest private investment in Warren County history, construction slated to start 2026. Amazon describes the build as supporting AI compute (custom chips/servers). Part of Amazon's $25B Mississippi program; distinct from the Madison County (Canton/Project Atlas) sites. plannedPowerMW is a GridTilt estimate; no MW disclosed.

clusters.name: AWS Clinton (Hinds County) Campus
clusters.notes: $1B AWS data center converting the former Delphi manufacturing plant in Clinton, Hinds County; ribbon-cutting / investment marked June 2026, timeline accelerated for faster construction. Largest private investment in Hinds County history, part of Amazon's $25B Mississippi AI/cloud program. Distinct from Madison and Warren county sites. plannedPowerMW is a conservative GridTilt estimate; no MW disclosed.

clusters.name: Meta Henrico Data Center
clusters.energySource: Solar (100% renewable matched, Virginia utility PPAs)
clusters.notes: In White Oak Technology Park, Sandston (Henrico County). Broke ground 2017, online from 2020. Seven-building campus, ~2.5M sq ft, $1.7B+ investment, powered 100% by solar via Virginia utility PPAs. ratedPowerMW is a conservative GridTilt estimate for a multi-building campus this size; no official campus MW disclosed.

clusters.name: Meta Gallatin Data Center
clusters.energySource: Renewable (TVA PPAs, 530 MW new renewables in TN)
clusters.notes: North of Nashville. Went live Nov 2024; $1.5B+ total investment, LEED Gold. Reported drawing up to ~300 MW. Meta has also deployed rapid-build 'tent' AI structures in Tennessee near Gallatin in 2026. ratedPowerMW is a sourced approximation of campus draw.

clusters.name: Meta Forest City Data Center
clusters.notes: 1275 North Community Circle. Opened 2012; second-phase three-building expansion added ~1.5M sq ft in 2023. Forest City reportedly used ~30 MW in 2024 for older halls; ratedPowerMW raised to ~60 MW as conservative estimate after the multi-building expansion. Five-building campus.

clusters.name: Meta Prineville Data Center Campus
clusters.notes: Meta's first owned data center (online April 2011) and birthplace of Open Compute Project. Multi-building campus (DCs 1-6+); Meta operates ~10 sites in the Bend-Prineville market (483 MW total across all operators). ratedPowerMW is a conservative campus estimate; no single official Meta campus MW disclosed.

clusters.name: Meta Sarpy Data Center
clusters.energySource: Wind (100% renewable; Dixon County NE wind)
clusters.notes: Spans Papillion and Springfield in Sarpy County. Online 2019; expanding to a nine-building, ~4M sq ft campus, $1.5B+ investment, 100% wind-matched. No official MW disclosed; rated/planned MW are GridTilt estimates for a campus of this scale.

clusters.name: Meta Kuna Data Center
clusters.energySource: Renewable (100% renewable; +200 MW new renewables in ID)
clusters.notes: Suburb of Boise (Treasure Valley). Announced Feb 2022, ~960,000 sq ft, ~$1B investment, completed ~2025. Meta added 200 MW of new renewables in Idaho. ratedPowerMW/plannedPowerMW are conservative GridTilt estimates; no official campus MW disclosed.

clusters.name: Meta Rosemount Data Center
clusters.notes: AI-optimized data center at UMore Park (former WWII gunpowder site), Dakota County. $800M, 715,000 sq ft on 280 acres; Meta's 23rd global data center. Officially stated to require ~700 MW of power; 100% renewable via Xcel Energy. Targeted open 2026.

clusters.name: Meta Cheyenne Data Center
clusters.energySource: Renewable incl. wind (Black Hills Energy grid additions)
clusters.notes: Announced July 2024: $800M+, 715,000 sq ft on a 960-acre site, explicitly optimized for AI workloads. Construction on first building began early 2024; scheduled to open by 2027. Working with Black Hills Energy on new grid resources incl. renewables/wind. plannedPowerMW is a GridTilt estimate for a 715k sq ft AI campus.

clusters.name: Meta Huntsville Data Center
clusters.notes: Announced 2018, began serving traffic ~2021; $1.5B campus investment with added buildings and 300+ operational jobs. Supported by 377 MW TVA solar + 227 MW First Solar (Colbert County) + 150 MW NextEra deals. A later expansion was paused amid Meta's AI redesign pivot. ratedPowerMW is a conservative campus estimate.

clusters.name: Meta Los Lunas Data Center
clusters.energySource: Solar + wind + BESS (885 MW contracted renewables, 100 MW storage; 150 MW geothermal PPA)
clusters.notes: ~750-acre desert campus, online from 2019. Seven operational buildings + three under construction; ~3.8M sq ft, each hall ~40 MW draw. ~$3.3B total bet. Backed by 885 MW contracted solar/wind across six NM counties, 100 MW BESS, plus a 150 MW XGS geothermal PPA (by 2030). ratedPowerMW estimated from ~7 halls x 40 MW.

clusters.name: Meta Mesa Data Center
clusters.energySource: Solar (450 MW new solar in AZ; 100% renewable-matched)
clusters.notes: Maricopa County, 3841 S. Ellsworth Rd, 396-acre site. Meta's 23rd US / 27th global facility; came online 2025. Phase one = two buildings (~970,000 sq ft) operational; planned five-building campus ($1B+). Originally slated 2023, delayed during Meta's AI-redesign pause. 450 MW new AZ solar; 100% renewable-matched. Power figures are GridTilt estimates.

clusters.name: Lambda AI Factory - Kansas City
clusters.notes: Former Bank of America DC campus at 11155 N. Airworld Drive, Kansas City (Platte County/Northland). 259,110 sq ft across two buildings, 16.9 acres. Launching early 2026 at 24 MW with >10,000 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs (disclosed count), scalable to 100+ MW and double the GPUs. gpuCount = announced initial figure; plannedPowerMW = announced max scale.

clusters.name: Lambda at Prime LAX01 - Vernon
clusters.notes: Lambda leasing 21 MW (of LAX01's 33 MW total, 242,000 sq ft, six data halls) at Prime Data Centers' flagship LAX01 campus in Vernon, CA. NVIDIA Blackwell for training/fine-tuning/inference, air or liquid cooled; powered by Vernon Public Utilities. Announced Nov 2025, deployment progressing as of early 2026. plannedPowerMW reflects Lambda's leased portion.

clusters.name: Lambda at Aligned DFW-04 - Plano
clusters.notes: Aligned's DFW-04 at 401 N. Star Road, Plano (44 acres, 425,000 sq ft), $700M project. ~72 MW of compute power for Lambda, on-site substation, air + liquid cooling, supports NVIDIA Blackwell / Blackwell Ultra; completion 2026. (Aligned's '5,000 MW future capacity' line refers to its portfolio, not this site, so excluded.)

clusters.name: Lambda AI Factory at EdgeConneX - Chicago
clusters.notes: EdgeConneX build-to-density, single-tenant 23 MW data center for Lambda in Chicago, Ready-for-Service 2026. Hybrid liquid-to-chip + air cooling, EdgeConneX Ingenuity, >600 kW/rack. Part of a 30+ MW Lambda/EdgeConneX two-city program (Chicago + Atlanta).

clusters.name: CoreWeave Lancaster AI Data Center
clusters.notes: $6B CoreWeave AI campus on former LSC Communications/R.R. Donnelley printing plants (1.5M sq ft, 144 acres). Initial 100MW with expansion to 300MW. $4B JV financing via Blue Owl Capital, Chirisa Technology Parks (CTP), Machine Investment Group (MIG); built by Turner-Wohlsen JV. Phase 1 operational Q1 2027. Pre-construction/early construction so ratedPowerMW=0; planned uses data-center MW not generation.

clusters.name: CoreWeave Kenilworth (NEST) Data Center
clusters.notes: ~$1.8B, 392,600 sq ft AI data center on Onyx's Northeast Science & Technology Center (NEST, former Merck campus, building 11 NEST). 250MW capacity. CoreWeave bought facility + 27 acres for $322M. First award under NJ EDA data-center tax credit ($50M/yr cap). Construction began mid-Sep 2025; operational early 2027. Under construction so ratedPowerMW=0.

clusters.name: Core Scientific Denton HPC Data Center
clusters.notes: Former Core Scientific bitcoin-mining site at 8171 Jim Christal Rd converted to GPU HPC, leased to CoreWeave (OpenAI workloads). >16,000 GPUs installed by end-Dec 2025. +70MW contracted brings full critical IT load to ~260MW; conservative current rated ~190MW (operational, partial buildout) marked estimated. Up to $6.1B campus plan. Distinct from any existing CoreWeave-owned campus; this is the Core Scientific Denton site.

clusters.name: Core Scientific Muskogee HPC Data Center
clusters.notes: Core Scientific + CoreWeave broke ground on 100MW HPC facility in Port of Muskogee Industrial Park (~70MW critical IT load). Existing 70MW leased facility built for NVIDIA GB300, in final commissioning, delivery Q2 2026. Long-term plan to scale campus to ~1.5GW gross (~1GW leasable). planned = data-center MW (combining new-build + GB300 leased phase, ~170MW near-term), not the 1.5GW pipeline. Pre-completion so ratedPowerMW=0.

clusters.name: Nebius Vineland (New Jersey) AI Data Center
clusters.notes: Nebius US region in Vineland NJ, built on DataOne (landlord/host) infrastructure under 10-yr tenant commitment; first phase delivered in ~20 weeks (summer 2025), expandable to 300MW (and a stated potential further +400MW). ~85% self-generated power via natural gas (behind-the-meter), with LNG backup tank sought. Microsoft is a named GPU-capacity tenant. planned uses compute MW (300MW data center), not gas generation. Status construction/early online so ratedPowerMW=0 conservatively.

clusters.name: Lambda at EdgeConneX Chicago AI Factory
clusters.notes: EdgeConneX building a single-tenant 23MW high-density AI Factory in Chicago for Lambda (Ready-for-Service 2026), part of 30MW+ Chicago+Atlanta program. Liquid-to-chip + air hybrid cooling, 600kW+/rack (EdgeConneX Ingenuity). EdgeConneX is landlord/operator; Lambda is tenant. planned=23MW (the disclosed Chicago tranche). Pre-RFS so ratedPowerMW=0.

clusters.name: Voltage Park at Centeris (Puyallup)
clusters.notes: Voltage Park GPU-cloud deployment (10+MW) at Centeris data center, 1023 39th Ave SE, Puyallup WA (Tacoma-Pierce County); clean hydroelectric power, water cooling, sales/use tax exemption. Centeris facility has 42.5MW utility power total; Voltage Park's tranche is 10+MW (rated marked estimated). Centeris is landlord; Voltage Park is operator/tenant. Bringing additional B200 GPUs online in western WA.

clusters.name: Vultr Springfield AI Supercluster
clusters.notes: Vultr 50MW AI supercluster with 24,000 AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs at Prime Ohio corporate park (former LexisNexis data center), landlord/operator 5C (5c). Building scaled 67,000 -> 214,000 sq ft; up to $1B-$1.3B investment; online early 2026. planned=50MW disclosed cluster. Pre-completion so ratedPowerMW=0.

clusters.name: Denvr Dataworks Houston (HOU1)
clusters.notes: Denvr's US South region (HOU1, Houston TX): operational AI cloud offering 8x H100 80GB SXM, A100, and Gaudi 2 instances; disclosed Nvidia HGX H100 cluster of 1,024 SXM5 GPUs on Quantum-2 InfiniBand. No power figure disclosed; rated/planned 10MW is a conservative GridTilt estimate for a ~1,000-H100 deployment (marked estimated). Smaller real AI-cloud campus.

clusters.name: MARA Hannibal (Long Ridge) AI Campus
clusters.notes: MARA is acquiring the 505MW Long Ridge combined-cycle gas plant in Hannibal, OH (~$1.5B) on 1,600+ acres to build an AI/HPC data-center campus. Initial 200MW of IT load targeted operational by mid-2028, expandable to ~600MW of compute. Power-plant generation (505MW) is NOT used as compute MW; planned compute figure (600MW) is the announced full data-center buildout. Pre-construction, so ratedPowerMW 0.

clusters.name: Cipher Barber Lake AI Campus
clusters.notes: Cipher's Barber Lake site in Colorado City (Mitchell County), West Texas. Fluidstack signed a 10-year HPC colocation lease, expanded to lease the entire 300MW of capacity (initially 168MW critical IT / 244MW gross). Google backstops $1.4B of Fluidstack's lease obligations. Site in development/construction; ratedPowerMW 0 pre-energization. plannedPowerMW = 300MW full data-center buildout.

clusters.name: Cipher Stingray AI Data Center
clusters.notes: Cipher's Stingray site in Andrews County, TX (250 acres, 100MW front-of-meter), targeted for AI/HPC use with AWS as tenant per SEC filings; financed via an $810M senior secured notes offering. Expected to energize ~Q2 2026. Pre-energization so ratedPowerMW 0; ~70MW critical IT load reported, 100MW gross planned.

clusters.name: Soluna Project Kati AI/HPC Campus
clusters.notes: Soluna's Project Kati in Willacy County, TX (Rio Grande Valley near Raymondville), wind-powered (Las Majadas Wind PPA). Kati 1 (83MW) energized Feb 2026; 166MW planned across two phases split Bitcoin/AI. Soluna signed an MoU with Metrobloks to co-develop 100MW+ of dense GPU AI/HPC capacity at the campus, with future expansion beyond 300MW. ratedPowerMW (83) is the energized first phase; plannedPowerMW (300) is the announced AI/HPC expansion target.

clusters.name: Switch Las Vegas Core Campus (EVO AI Factories)
clusters.notes: Switch's flagship Las Vegas Core Campus, Rob Roy's EVO AI Factories. Site of CoreWeave's industry-first NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 liquid-cooled deployment (with Dell/Vertiv), announced July 2025. ~275MW operational today (rated MW estimated as current operational capacity); planned up to ~495MW at full build-out. AI factories designed for >2MW per cabinet.

clusters.name: Switch Grand Rapids (The Pyramid Campus)
clusters.notes: Switch's Eastern US Tier 5 campus in West Michigan (adaptive reuse of Steelcase Pyramid plus additional buildings). Marketed as an AI/cloud/enterprise campus supporting high-density GPU. Planned build-out up to ~1.8M sq ft and ~320MW; rated MW is a conservative operational estimate. Switch markets liquid cooling and AI-ready capacity across all five US exascale campuses.

clusters.name: Switch Atlanta (The Keep Campus)
clusters.notes: Switch's Tier 5 Platinum exascale campus in metro Atlanta (Lithia Springs). Supports high density up to 55kW+ per cabinet; planned to ~1.1M sq ft and ~150MW with a 2,000+ acre adjacent expansion for multi-gigawatt growth. Rated MW is a conservative operational estimate. AI-ready colocation.

clusters.name: EdgeConneX / Lambda Chicago AI Factory
clusters.notes: Announced Aug 2025. Single-tenant, build-to-density 23MW AI data center for Lambda using EdgeConneX 'Ingenuity' platform (hybrid liquid-to-chip + air, >600kW/rack capable), ready for NVIDIA GB300 NVL72. Ready-for-Service targeted 2026. Part of Lambda's 2GW+ / 1M+ GPU build-out vision.

clusters.name: DataBank Red Oak Campus
clusters.notes: Dallas-area campus: 292 acres, eight buildings, 480MW, ~3.4M sq ft. Funded via DataBank's $2B equity raise (led by AustralianSuper) explicitly to meet AI demand. Phased build with first deliveries through mid-2026. Part of DataBank's plan to triple power capacity (+850MW) across US markets.

clusters.name: Flexential Plano (CoreWeave high-density)
clusters.notes: Flexential delivered 13MW of contiguous high-density colocation in Plano for CoreWeave's GPU/AI deployment (announced end of April 2025). Flexential is an NVIDIA DGX-Ready provider supporting >80kW/cabinet. Part of the Flexential-CoreWeave alliance (other CoreWeave sites at Hillsboro OR and Douglasville GA, ~9MW each).

clusters.name: Cologix COL4 Scalelogix (Columbus, Lambda B200)
clusters.notes: Cologix COL4 Scalelogix hyperscale-edge data center in Columbus: 33MW across three halls, 256,000 sq ft. Hosts Lambda's NVIDIA HGX B200 AI clusters (first B200-accelerated clusters in the region). Connected via dark fiber to COL1-3 (<0.5ms) for LLM training/inference scaling. First completed AI-ready colocation DC in the Columbus market.

clusters.name: Cologix Johnstown Ohio AI Campus
clusters.notes: Cologix's new AI-ready Central Ohio campus on ~154 acres in Johnstown: eight AI-ready data centers, up to 800MW scalable, ~2.0M sq ft, >$7B investment. First phase development anticipated to begin 2025. Distinct land/campus from its existing Columbus Scalelogix sites.

clusters.name: CloudHQ Ashburn LC Campus
clusters.notes: CloudHQ's flagship US hyperscale campus in Ashburn (Loudoun County), Data Center Alley. Planned ~14 buildings with combined critical IT load ~1,228MW (some sources cite >1.7GW total). Individual buildings (e.g., LC4) ~180MW; rated MW reflects a single delivered building as a conservative operational figure. AI/hyperscale-focused.

clusters.name: STACK South Dallas Campus (Lancaster)
clusters.notes: STACK's flagship South Dallas campus in Lancaster: 220MW across six 36MW buildings on 100 acres, ~1.5M sq ft, committed power from Oncor via dedicated substation. Designed with flexible cooling for AI/cloud high-density workloads; mid-2026 delivery target.

clusters.name: Aligned PHX-13 (Glendale)
clusters.notes: Aligned broke ground on PHX-13, a 72MW facility and the first of four planned data centers on a 100-acre Glendale AZ campus. Built for AI/HPC with Aligned's DeltaFlow liquid cooling (supports any density / GPU cloud) and Delta3 air arrays, closed-loop water recycling, Adaptive Modular Infrastructure.

clusters.name: Compass Hoffman Estates Campus (former Sears HQ)
clusters.notes: 5 hyperscale buildings (each >250k sqft) on ~200-acre former Sears HQ site at 3333 Beverly Rd, powered by ComEd. $10B project. First building powered mid-2026. MW not officially confirmed; plannedPowerMW 200 is a conservative GridTilt estimate based on Compass' ~40MW/building reporting (some sources cite up to 500MW). Construction underway, no building online yet.

clusters.name: T5 Chicago IV (Grayslake) Campus
clusters.notes: AI-ready campus ~40 miles north of Chicago on 140-160 acres, up to 1.2GW IT across ~20 buildings (60MW each), backed by 1.6GW secured ComEd utility power. Phase 1 = three 60MW buildings (180MW) targeted Q4 2027. Pre-construction, ratedPowerMW 0.

clusters.name: CyrusOne Bosque County Campus (Thad Hill)
clusters.notes: AI-ready hyperscale campus in Bosque County (near Whitney TX) on Calpine Thad Hill Energy Center powered land. Initial 190MW agreement (Jul 2025) expanded +210MW (Nov 2025) to ~400MW total; $1.2B investment. Phase 1 >190,000 sqft under construction, online Q4 2026. plannedPowerMW 400 reflects the contracted DC power, not power-plant generation. No building energized yet, ratedPowerMW 0.

clusters.name: NTT Mesa Campus (PH2)
clusters.notes: NTT's second Phoenix-area campus: 173-acre site at Pecos & Crismon roads in Mesa, 7 buildings ~1.7M sqft, 360MW, closed-loop water cooling for AI workloads. Land acquired for $300M; first building targeted Nov 2028. Pre-construction, ratedPowerMW 0.

clusters.name: Yondr Lancaster Campus
clusters.notes: 163-acre site in Lancaster TX (south of Dallas) to accommodate 550MW critical IT load, hyperscale/AI. Construction expected to begin 2026; tenant undisclosed. Pre-construction, ratedPowerMW 0.

clusters.name: Digital Realty Aurora AI Factory (Manassas)
clusters.notes: 96MW 'Aurora AI Factory' at Digital Realty's Manassas (Northern Virginia) campus, home to NVIDIA's AI Factory Research Center and the Omniverse DSX blueprint; advanced liquid cooling for gigascale AI. Announced Nov 3, 2025, completion targeted H1 2026. chipType NVIDIA (research center); no GPU count disclosed. Under construction, ratedPowerMW 0 until online.

clusters.name: Sailfish Kyle Campus
clusters.notes: Sailfish four-building, 800 MW data-center campus outside Austin in Kyle, TX, with on-site power generation to meet part of demand. 800 MW is the data-center capacity. No online date disclosed.

clusters.name: Sailfish New Braunfels Campus
clusters.energySource: Mix of on-site, behind-the-meter, and grid
clusters.notes: Sailfish eight-building, 800 MW data-center campus on 196 acres outside Austin in New Braunfels, TX, powered by a mix of on-site, behind-the-meter, and grid sources. 800 MW is the DC/compute capacity. No online date disclosed.

clusters.name: Sailfish Social Circle Campus
clusters.notes: Sailfish four-building, 800 MW (1.78M sq ft) data-center campus on 344 acres in the Atlanta-area town of Social Circle, GA. 800 MW is the DC/compute figure. Part of Sailfish's pipeline of campuses sited adjacent to existing gas and nuclear generation. No online date disclosed.

clusters.name: CloudBurst San Marcos Data Center I
clusters.energySource: On-site natural gas via Energy Transfer Oasis Pipeline (behind-the-meter)
clusters.notes: AI/HPC data-center campus in the San Marcos / New Braunfels corridor (Hays/Guadalupe Counties), between Austin and San Antonio. Master-planned for up to 1.2 GW of AI/HPC data-center capacity; first 50 MW phase scheduled live Q4 2026. Powered by on-site natural gas via a 10-year Energy Transfer Oasis Pipeline deal (gas sufficient for ~1.8 GW of generation). plannedPowerMW = 1.2 GW data-center/compute capacity, not the 1.8 GW generation figure.

clusters.name: EdgeCore Culpeper Campus
clusters.notes: 120-acre, 1.4M sq ft hyperscale campus in Culpeper Tech Zone (acquired from Cielo). Initially 196-216MW critical IT, scaling to 432MW. First power early 2028. Closed-loop air cooling, WUE <0.01 L/kWh.

clusters.name: Culpeper Technology Campus
clusters.notes: 150-acre, ~2.05-2.1M sq ft campus, eight buildings, in Culpeper Tech Zone. Powered by two approved 300MW Dominion substations (600MW). Approved 2023; power expected Q1 2027.

clusters.name: CloudHQ CLP Campus
clusters.notes: 100-acre CLP campus on McDevitt Drive, Culpeper; three data centers totaling ~954,000 sq ft to up to 2.1M sq ft. Reported ~275MW load (142MW critical). Hyperscale.

clusters.name: Copper Ridge Data Center Campus
clusters.notes: 116-acre campus in Culpeper Tech Zone, up to eight two-story buildings (2.36M sq ft) plus on-site substation; ~600MW at full build-out. Approved 2023; developer St. Mawes via CR1/CR2 Culpeper LLC.

clusters.name: Gainesville Crossing Data Campus
clusters.notes: 130-acre, ~326MW campus, five two-story buildings (2.3M sq ft) on I-66 in Prince William County. First 72MW building delivered May 2024, second 72MW underway, third 54MW started Jan 2025. Rated estimate reflects two ~72MW buildings live.

clusters.name: Gigaland / Remington Innovation Campus
clusters.notes: Gigaland LLC's ~200-acre campus south of Remington, Fauquier County. Resubmitted scaled-down plan: six buildings, ~998,662 sq ft, two 300MW substations (600MW), down from original 1.2GW/seven buildings. Pre-approval.

clusters.name: Yondr Loudoun Campus
clusters.notes: Hyperscale campus in Loudoun County developed with JK Land Holdings. First 48MW building RFS; 96MW two-building campus with second building ramping to full service 2026. Further 240MW pipeline on adjacent parcel brings total to 336MW. Waterless design.

clusters.name: Rowan Bauxite (Frederick) Campus
clusters.notes: Bauxite I campus within the 2,100-acre Quantum Frederick (former Alcoa Eastalco) park, Frederick County MD. Four single-story buildings, 777,150 sq ft on 151 acres, 231MW, on-site Potomac Edison substation. $975M construction financing closed. Bauxite II/III also approved.

clusters.name: Aligned Maryland (Quantum Frederick) Campus
clusters.notes: Aligned's 75-acre campus within TPG's Quantum Frederick park, Frederick County MD. Four buildings totaling 264MW (IAD-04 through IAD-07); IAD-06 (72MW, 450,000 sq ft) structurally topped out. Hyperscale/AI buildout.

clusters.name: Project Sail (Coweta County)
clusters.notes: 900MW campus on 832 acres in Coweta County (near Newnan, ~45 mi south of Atlanta). 4.34M sq ft, nine buildings, ~$17B. Announced by Atlas Development Jan 2025; Prologis agreed to buy the site May 2025. Rezoning approved by Coweta County.

clusters.name: QTS Fayetteville Campus (Project Excalibur)
clusters.notes: 615-acre campus south of Atlanta, up to 16 buildings, ~6.6M sq ft of data center space. Reported power capacity figures range 250-500MW (used conservative 500MW; estimated). Construction began 2023, full build-out targeted ~2032.

clusters.name: CloudHQ SAT Campus
clusters.notes: 123-acre campus at Texas Research Park (west Bexar County, former UT Health Science Center site), up to 600MW critical IT load across four or five multi-story data centers. Multiple onsite substations, four diverse fiber paths. CloudHQ acquired the land June 2023.

clusters.name: EdgeCore Mesa Campus
clusters.notes: Metro Phoenix campus in Mesa; first campus established April 2023 with 206MW constructed and commissioned (rated/operational figure). Acquired adjacent 43.87 acres to expand to 450MW+, two more buildings completing 2025-2026. Air-cooled, near-zero water; power via Salt River Project. $1.9B financing led by TD Securities.
